tests.name: Effective description
tests.reasoning: The description starts with 'Use this skill when the user wants...' which is imperative phrasing focused on user intent. It explicitly lists many trigger contexts (high bill, idle PT, quota headroom, pricing tiers, token drift, pasted CloudWatch/Cost Explorer output) covering cases where the user doesn't name the domain directly, and also states a clear exclusion ('Not for outages happening now'). While long, it is a single dense paragraph of trigger phrases rather than verbose prose, consistent with being 'pushy' about scope coverage as the best practice encourages.
tests.evidence: Use this skill when the user wants to understand or cut Amazon Bedrock spend, or check Bedrock capacity, even if they don't call it a cost review, for example why the bill is high or suspiciously low... Not for outages happening now.

tests.name: Verbosity and conciseness
tests.reasoning: The body is dense but almost entirely domain-specific — rules about billed vs estimated labeling, token reconciliation, quota codes, etc. It does not explain general concepts the agent already knows (e.g., what Cost Explorer is, what a token is).
tests.evidence: "Label every dollar figure. `(billed)`: read from Cost Explorer, with the grouping and service names... `(estimated)`: tokens × published prices..."

tests.name: Detailed reference materials must not be in body
tests.reasoning: Detailed lookup tables (quota codes, metric thresholds, check catalogs) are factored into references/ files and only a compact router table and check-id summary table remain in the body, which are necessary for navigation rather than deep reference data.
tests.evidence: "How to read each API and metric: [collection-reference.md](references/collection-reference.md) (load it with any row)."

tests.name: Reference files must be linked
tests.reasoning: All eight reference files (api-quirks.md, checks-model-invocation.md, cloudwatch-alarm-reference.md, collection-reference.md, cost-analysis.md, metrics-and-logs.md, quota-codes.md, related-skills.md) are linked via markdown links in the body.

tests.name: Reference links must specify when to load
tests.reasoning: Each reference link is tied to a specific triggering condition or step, e.g. load collection-reference with any row, load cost-analysis before LLM-COST/PT findings, load quota-codes before GetServiceQuota.
tests.evidence: "[cost-analysis.md](references/cost-analysis.md) (Steps 3–5, before any LLM-COST or LLM-PT finding)"

tests.name: Reference path format
tests.reasoning: All reference links use relative paths of the form references/<filename>.md with no absolute paths or traversals.

tests.name: Prescription vs description
tests.reasoning: Fragile, correctness-critical operations (billed vs estimated labeling, token reconciliation, quota lookups) are given exact, prescriptive rules, while more flexible judgment calls (deciding COST-003/004 applicability, scoping defaults) are left with guidance and rationale rather than rigid steps.
tests.evidence: "Never a rate from memory, a launch post or 'the same price as the previous generation'..." vs "decide 003/004 from the invocation pattern and the stated workload, at catalog severity."

tests.name: Defaults, not menus
tests.reasoning: Where multiple rate sources or data paths exist, the skill specifies an explicit order/default (e.g., rates: user, then pricing:GetProducts, then pricing page) rather than presenting equal options.
tests.evidence: "**Rates**, in order: the user (say so); `pricing:GetProducts` ... or the [pricing page]... read with `verify_aws_claim`."

tests.name: Favor procedures over declarations
tests.reasoning: The procedure teaches a generalizable method for any Bedrock cost/capacity review (scope, tokens, cost model, coverage check, checks, PT, headroom, alarms) rather than a one-off instance, while including reusable templates and check-ids as specific details within that generalizable approach.
tests.evidence: "Run the steps in order. Each step is bounded: a denied API, no datapoints or an unsupported region is recorded as `unavailable` / `not checked` and the review goes on."

tests.name: Gotchas section
tests.reasoning: The skill has an extensive 'Common wrong answers' section plus 'Error Handling' with API quirks that function as gotchas, documenting concrete non-obvious pitfalls like ACTIVE != in use, us. profile billing, quota burndown math.
tests.evidence: "**"A `us.` profile bills as us-east-1."** It is a geographic routing scope; billing follows the source region..."

tests.name: Templates and outputs missing
tests.reasoning: The skill provides an output template reference for the full report, satisfying the need for structured output.

tests.name: Templates and outputs must not be in body
tests.reasoning: No large inline output template exists in the body; the report template is correctly offloaded to assets/ and only referenced.
tests.evidence: Body contains no inline report skeleton beyond a small quota table format; the full template lives in assets/capacity-cost-report-template.md.

tests.name: Asset files must be linked
tests.reasoning: The single asset file capacity-cost-report-template.md is linked in the body.

tests.name: Asset links must specify when to load
tests.reasoning: The asset link specifies it should be loaded only for a full report, giving a clear condition for when to use it.

tests.name: Asset path format
tests.reasoning: The asset reference uses a relative path from the skill root with no traversal or absolute path.

tests.name: Step-by-step guidance
tests.reasoning: The procedural 'Procedure — Capacity & Cost Review' section is correctly formatted as an ordered checkbox checklist with 'Step N:' naming, and sub-sections consistently reference those step numbers (e.g., Step 2b, Step 3b).

tests.name: Validation loops
tests.reasoning: The skill includes an explicit self-validation section instructing the agent to check its own output against rules before presenting.
tests.evidence: "## Before You Present — Validate Your Own Output\n\nA confidently wrong cost number is worse than a slow one. If an item can't be met, say so."
